Scope: Abrupt Firefox exit during an incomplete one-use POST response after native prepare but before cancellation/commit
Findings: A 64 KiB held prefix did not produce observable Firefox progress; first attempt stopped before termination.
With a 1 MiB prefix, the browser reported partial progress and was terminated and relaunched.
Server observed the original 49-byte POST followed by a GET to the same one-use URL; the second request was rejected with 410.
After restart Firefox reported a completed zero-byte item with a new start time; only a zero-byte output file remained.
UDM capture-status failed with an acknowledgement timeout; the journal stayed preparing through the 35-second recovery observation.
Native catalog retained the prepared protected request and had no admitted download job.
Observer recorded no extension pause/resume call.
Limitations: The extra GET was observed across browser restart; its precise Firefox initiation path was not instrumented.
No IDM reference crash test, so this is a UDM acceptance gap, not a demonstrated comparative IDM advantage.
Physical power loss and longer alarm-based recovery are not qualified.
NextWork: Qualify native reconnection and retry after browser-owned host termination.
Preserve an explicit user recovery decision for an incomplete response without automatically replaying the protected POST.
Prevent an unverified zero-byte browser result from being treated as proof the handoff completed.
